To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a PDZ protein domain was computationally designed from scratch and that the resulting sequences were expressed in bacteria and showed native-like properties.

we have used computational protein design to entirely redesign a PDZ domain using a physics-based energy function that combines molecular mechanics and a continuum electrostatics solvent model, that the three lowest-energy designs that we chose for experimental testing were all overexpressed and exhibited native-like circular dichromism and 1-D NMR spectra, and that two of the designs exhibited upshift of their denaturation curves upon binding a peptide ligand, suggesting that these designs had folded properly.
a physics-based energy function can be used for the whole-protein computational redesign of a protein, and that this energy function is sufficient to generate a protein that binds its ligand.
